subject: Price mirroring request + operational fit questions
messages:
From: Lydia Park <lydia@pegasushealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Aaron Lee <aaron.lee@pegasushealth.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing question — can Redwood mirror incumbent offer?

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We like Redwood's performance profile, but finance pushed back on list pricing when we compared it to our incumbent vendor.

Two quick asks:
1) Can Redwood "mirror" the incumbent effective unit price for the first 12 months (we're looking at per-token plus embedding units)?
2) What packaging options do you recommend for a 4-team pilot (about 12 engineers + 5 product seats) — should we go committed throughput or seat-based, and how does that affect SLA/latency guarantees?

We have an internal deadline next Friday to decide which vendor to pick for the pilot. If you can send a proposal with the comparable economics and any migration/onramp credits you can offer, that would help.

Appreciate it —
Lydia
Director of AI Systems
Pegasus Health

--
Attachment: incumbent-pricing-summary.csv (referenced)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Lydia Park <lydia@pegasushealth.com>
Cc: Aaron Lee <aaron.lee@pegasushealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing question — can Redwood mirror incumbent offer?

Hi Lydia — thanks for the clear asks and for the fast timeline. Summary up front: we can offer a limited 12-month price-mirroring arrangement with conditions (committed spend + migration credit) and a packaging recommendation that balances predictability and latency. See details below and attached workbook (redwood_price_mirror_proposal.xlsx).

Proposal highlights:
- Price mirror window: 12 months from go-live date if Pegasus commits to $300k committed spend over 12 months (usage commitment).
- Mirror scope: text-generation per-token rate and embeddings units only; additional premium for Dedicated GPU pools or guaranteed sub-50ms p95 latency (see SLA delta table in attachment).
- Onramp credit: $40k one-time credit to offset egress and migration work (applied as invoice credit).
- Packaging recommendation: for a 4-team pilot we recommend a hybrid: capped committed throughput (to preserve unit economics) + 15 product seats on hosted console for rapid onboarding. This keeps latency SLOs for user-facing endpoints while keeping cost predictable.

Operational notes:
- Dedicated capacity (if requested) adds a 25% fee on top of mirrored unit rates due to reserved GPU cost and SLA uplift.
- If Pegasus wants strict per-route latency SLAs sub-50ms p95 at 99.9% uptime, we require a dedicated pool or guaranteed burst reservations (see SLA summary PDF).
- We can include a rollback clause: if performance regressions occur or model parity issues are found, Redwood will fund a remediation sprint up to $15k during the first 90 days.

Next steps — can you confirm: (a) target go-live week, (b) preferred packaging (hosted hybrid vs dedicated), and (c) PO/contract owner? If you confirm by EOD Thursday we'll prioritize the redlines and get a DocuSign out.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: redwood_price_mirror_proposal.xlsx, redwood_sla_summary.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 11:17:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Pricing question — can Redwood mirror incumbent offer?

Karthik — quick notes from pricing: the $300k commit with $40k onramp credit is within concession guidelines for a mid-market deal but we should tighten the SLA uplift language. Two suggestions:

1) Replace the flat 25% dedicated uplift with a banded approach: +15% for shared dedicated pool (soft guarantee) and +30% for single-tenant reserved nodes (hard guarantee). Helps preserve margin if they insist on strict latency.
2) Cap the remediation sprint at 40 engineering hours (approx $12k) and require an ops root-cause appendix before funding.

If they accept the banded uplift and the commit level, we can approve pricing and push the DocuSign. If they push for seat-based licenses only (no commit), we should hold — seat-only commitments don't give us the unit economics needed to mirror their per-token price.

Also include a short break-out in the workbook: (a) immediate ARR impact, (b) 6-month unit economics with prefix caching assumptions. I updated the spreadsheet tab called 'Concession_approval'.

Marissa
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Lydia Park <lydia@pegasushealth.com>
Cc: Aaron Lee <aaron.lee@pegasushealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 03 Oct 2026 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing question — can Redwood mirror incumbent offer?

Hi Lydia — following up with an updated, approvable package. High level: we can match the incumbent unit economics for 12 months under the $300k commitment with the hybrid packaging and the banded dedicated uplift. Details: see attached (redwood_price_mirror_proposal.xlsx).

Concession summary (final):
- Commit: $300,000 over 12 months (billed monthly).
- Onramp credit: $40,000 applied as invoice credit in month 1.
- Mirror scope: per-token generation + embedding units for workloads migrated during pilot.
- Dedicated uplift: +15% (shared dedicated pool) or +30% (single-tenant reserved nodes) to the mirrored unit rate if they opt for guaranteed sub-50ms p95 latency.
- Rollback/remediation: capped at 40 hours (approx $12k) and conditioned on ops RCA sign-off.
- Packaging: hybrid (committed throughput cap + 15 product seats) recommended for best mix of predictability and developer velocity.

Next steps: if Pegasus confirms commit and preferred latency option by Tue 06 Oct, I'll generate a short-form SOW and a DocuSign offer (pre-filled with the bands above). I attached a one-page SLA summary and the pricing workbook.

Thanks for the quick turn — happy to jump on a 30-minute call if Aaron wants a line-by-line walk-through later today.

Best,
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0198
